name: PF-08653945
lead: PF-08653945 (also MET-233i) is an investigational amylin analogue for weight management, listed as being developed by Pfizer. It is not approved and has no published human trial results in the sources reviewed.
It belongs to the amylin analogue class, which a 2026 narrative review describes as an emerging therapeutic approach to obesity complementing incretin-based drugs.[1]

paras: No studies found. A 2026 review covers amylin-based therapies in obesity more broadly, including early-phase trials of the class.[1]

refs.title: Amylin Analogs: The Next Major Class of Weight Loss Therapy: A Review of Experimental Data and Early-Phase Clinical Trials

card.summary: Pfizer's early-stage amylin analogue for obesity; nothing published on it yet.
card.note: Investigational only; no human data found.

quick.overview:
PF-08653945 is an experimental amylin analogue being developed for weight loss. No trials or results were found for it specifically.

Amylin analogues are a drug class reviewed in 2026 as a possible next step after GLP-1 drugs.
quick.mechanism: Amylin analogues mimic a pancreatic hormone involved in satiety and slowing of digestion.
quick.risks: Human safety data for this compound are not public. It is unapproved and not legitimately available.
